title: Level 5 Leadership
coreMove: Shift leadership from personal display to institution-first responsibility.
sourcePressure: The source centers the paradox of personal humility and fierce professional will, contrasted with celebrity leadership and shown through the window-and-mirror pattern around credit and blame.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version treats humility as being pleasant, invisible, or unwilling to make hard demands.

hook: humble brag as proof of character

exampleSpecs.audience: a new surgical chief facing a preventable complication
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the unit learns from the failure or protects senior reputations
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chief names the night nurse's catch that saved the child, then points to his own missed staffing decision on the complication timeline
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blue complication timeline clipped to an operating-room light handle

exampleSpecs.audience: a rescue boat captain whose team pulled three kayakers out before a squall
exampleSpecs.stakes: praise could harden into bravado before the next dangerous call
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain hands the commendation letter to the deckhand who spotted the current shift, then writes his own delayed launch call on the error board
exampleSpecs.firstImage: salt drying in white streaks on a rescue boat rail

exampleSpecs.audience: a managing partner whose firm just won a civic library project
exampleSpecs.stakes: the win can become either a star-partner myth or a stronger design institution
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the partner sends the press quote to the junior modeler whose access ramp solved the bid, then rejects his own glass-atrium idea in the redesign markup
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a basswood model with a removable access ramp on a drafting bench

exampleSpecs.audience: a provost cutting programs after a failed enrollment bet
exampleSpecs.stakes: students need a viable path more than administrators need a saved face
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the provost opens the forum by showing the enrollment bet she approved, then protects the welding lab that outperformed her favored initiative
exampleSpecs.firstImage: welding shields stacked beside a half-filled auditorium stage

exampleSpecs.audience: an incident commander praised for saving a ridge town
exampleSpecs.stakes: the next crew needs accurate learning, not a legend
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the commander writes the dozer operator's fuel-road call in the win column and his own late evacuation trigger in the lesson column
exampleSpecs.firstImage: ash dust on a plastic incident map sleeve

exampleSpecs.audience: a board chair after a risky programming season sells out
exampleSpecs.stakes: the orchestra can either chase donor attention or strengthen the institution's musical discipline
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chair redirects the donor toast toward the principal bassoonist's programming note, then cancels the vanity encore series she had wanted
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bassoon reed case lying beside a donor place card

skillTargets: identify window-and-mirror behavior in pressure moments
choose institution-first responses to credit and blame
spot celebrity leadership disguised as decisiveness

tryThisNowSpec: Take one current win or miss. Write who gets public credit for the win and what decision you personally own in the miss.

sourceAnchors.name: Level 5 leadership
sourceAnchors.detail: the source defines it as personal humility paired with professional will, aimed at the institution rather than the leader's image
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Level 5 leadership keeps the force and moves the spotlight off the self.
